violations.legal_explanation: Component 'agpl-scraper' (AGPL-3.0-only) is governed by a network copyleft license (AGPL-3.0/SSPL Section 13). Deploying or interacting with this component in a SAAS_HOSTED environment triggers mandatory disclosure of the complete Corresponding Source code of the entire service or distributed application.
violations.remediation_advice: Remove 'agpl-scraper' immediately or replace it with a permissive (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD-3-Clause) alternative such as 'httpx' (BSD-3-Clause) + 'beautifulsoup4' (MIT) or 'scrapy' (BSD-3-Clause). Isolating AGPL components behind an internal microservice may still trigger Section 13 network interaction obligations if user requests flow through it.
obligations: Disclose complete Corresponding Source code to all network/distributed users under AGPL-3.0
Or remove/replace the component prior to deployment

violations.legal_explanation: Model weight 'meta-llama/Llama-3-8B' (Llama-3-Community) imposes user-count and usage restrictions that require review against terms of service: (1) products or services exceeding 700 million Monthly Active Users (MAU) on the model release date require a separate commercial license from Meta; (2) mandatory 'Built with Llama' UI/documentation attribution; and (3) compliance with the Llama Acceptable Use Policy.
violations.remediation_advice: Verify that company/product scale is below the 700M MAU threshold, display 'Built with Meta Llama' prominently in product UI and documentation, and enforce the Llama Acceptable Use Policy. Otherwise, replace 'meta-llama/Llama-3-8B' with an Apache-2.0 model such as 'mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1' (Apache-2.0) or 'Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B' (Apache-2.0).
obligations: Confirm Monthly Active Users (MAU) did not exceed 700M on model release date
Display 'Built with Meta Llama' prominently on websites, UI, and documentation
Include Meta Llama Community License Agreement in distributions and notices
Enforce Meta Acceptable Use Policy in downstream terms

violations.legal_explanation: Component/Model weight 'lmsys/vicuna-13b-v1.5' (CC-BY-NC-4.0) carries a strict Non-Commercial restriction. Using 'lmsys/vicuna-13b-v1.5' for inference, fine-tuning, synthetic data generation, or production serving in a commercial context violates the license grant.
violations.remediation_advice: Replace 'lmsys/vicuna-13b-v1.5' with commercially permissive model weights or libraries (e.g., Apache-2.0 or MIT licensed weights) such as 'mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2' (Apache-2.0), or negotiate a direct commercial license with the rights holder.
obligations: Prohibited from any commercial use, revenue-generating SaaS inference, or commercial product integration

violations.legal_explanation: Model weight 'stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0' (OpenRAIL-M) permits commercial use but enforces mandatory Responsible AI behavioral use-case restrictions (Attachment A), including prohibitions on biometric surveillance/identification, medical diagnosis or clinical advice, administration of justice, and generating disinformation. These restrictions must legally flow down to all downstream users.
violations.remediation_advice: Audit your product features and Terms of Service to ensure 'stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0' is not used for restricted Attachment A domains (biometrics, medical diagnosis, law enforcement), and include the mandatory OpenRAIL Use-Based Restrictions in your user-facing Terms of Service. If unrestricted weights are required, switch to an Apache-2.0 alternative such as an Apache-2.0 licensed image generation model (e.g., 'black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell' under Apache-2.0).
obligations: Pass through OpenRAIL Attachment A Use-Based Restrictions in downstream Terms of Service / EULA
Ensure model is not used for medical diagnosis, biometric categorization, or law enforcement
Include OpenRAIL-M license notice and attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
